title: When Trackers Fail: VLM-Guided Verification and Recovery for Robust Video Object Segmentation
claim: Baseline tracker silently loses the target after a disruption and never recovers; our verify-and-recover framework keeps tracking it correctly.
layout: 3 rows by 5 columns, frame-indexed left-to-right, color-coded row labels
description: A 3×5 grid of video frames from a string orchestra performance, with frame indices (f0, f72, f203, f211, f215) labeled at the top of each column. The top row is ground truth (green label), the middle row is the SAM 3 baseline (red label), and the bottom row is the proposed method (blue label). In each row a violin held by a girl is overlaid with a colored mask: green for ground truth, red for SAM 3, blue for ours. At f0 and f72 all rows track the violin. By f203, f211 and f215 the SAM 3 row has no mask at all, so the target is lost. The ground truth and Ours rows keep the mask on the violin. The colored row labels and the missing red mask are what the eye notices first.
caption: Our proposed Dual-Agent framework recovers tracking errors made by the tracker. Rows show ground truth (top), the SAM3 baseline (middle), and our Dual-Agent framework (bottom).
abstract: Recent trackers built on foundation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) achieve strong performance by propagating object masks through memory. However, this strength is also a key source of failure: under occlusion, reappearance, or distractors, an incorrect prediction can enter the tracking loop and be propagated over time, resulting in persistent identity drift. Existing approaches seek to prevent such failures through improved memory and temporal modeling, but once a failure occurs, the tracker has no explicit mechanism to recognize or correct it. We address this gap with Dual-Agent, a failure-aware tracking framework that complements propagation with explicit verification and recovery. We address this gap with Dual-Agent, a failure-aware tracking framework that complements propagation with explicit verification and recovery. A vision-language verification agent first reasons over spatio-temporal context to determine whether the tracker is still following the target. When a failure is detected, a correction agent uses temporal context to recover the target before tracking continues. The correction agent is trained on real SAM3 failures, augmented with targeted identity-switch and distractor perturbations that expose it to challenging ambiguities during recovery. On LVOS-v2 and SecVOS, Dual-Agent improves SAM3 by 1.2 and 2.7 $J\&F$, respectively. Importantly, the proposed framework transfers without retraining to SAM2.1, SeC, and Cutie, as well as to long-term video object tracking benchmarks including LaSOT-ext, TNL2K, and VOT-LT2022. Our results show that explicitly reasoning about when tracking fails and how to recover provides a complementary path to robust tracking beyond improving propagation alone.
